summary: One month in the page for a day chosen by where it falls — a day to resume on, a delivery day — taking and returning a YYYY-MM-DD string.
useWhen: the day is chosen by looking at the month — which weekday, how far off — not recalled and typed
the calendar would otherwise be a second layer: inside a Modal or a SidePanel, where a DatePicker's popover opens over a dialog
the page has room for a month, and the day is the main question on it

useInstead.when: a date the person knows — a birthday, an invoice date — or a form with other fields
useInstead.why: typing a known date is faster than finding it, and a field takes one row where this takes a month
this holds one day; a range needs the band between its ends and a check that the end is not before the start

useInstead.when: a moment, with a time of day
useInstead.why: this is fixed to days; a moment's bound such as "not before now" needs the time too

useInstead.when: one of a few days the product defines — four delivery slots
useInstead.why: a choice from a short list, not a date; a month of which four days work reads as a month of refusals

composition.note: `label` names it, joined to the visible month. `value` is YYYY-MM-DD, or null for none yet; `onChange` gets YYYY-MM-DD and never null. Bound it with `minValue` and `maxValue`, and refuse single days with `isDateUnavailable`. With nothing selected it opens on today, or on `minValue` when today is before it, or on `defaultFocusedValue`.
composition.example: <Calendar label="Resume on" value={day} onChange={setDay} minValue={tomorrow} maxValue={inNinetyDays} description="At the start of the day, UTC." />

requires: a `label`: it is the calendar's name, and the only thing that says what the day is for
guarantees: named by `label` and then the visible month — "Resume on October 2026" — so paging months says where you are
arrow keys move by day and week, Page Up and Page Down by month, Home and End to the week's ends; Enter or Space picks the focused day
every day is named by its full date in the reader's language, with today and the selected day said as such; a newly picked day is announced
days before `minValue`, after `maxValue` or refused by `isDateUnavailable` cannot be picked, and the month arrows stop at the bounds
a value it refuses marks it invalid on its own — `errorMessage`, when given, replaces the description — and the frame turns to the error border
`description` or the error is the calendar's accessible description
disabled, it keeps showing the chosen day, on the disabled surface, and no day can be picked or moved to
notes: No clearing: a day is changed by picking another. Offer a separate control when "no day" is an answer.
Always one month; for two months side by side, the range is DateRangePicker's.

antiPatterns.dont: a Calendar for a date of birth or any date the person knows
antiPatterns.why: paging back decades through months is the worst way to enter a date someone can type in a second

antiPatterns.dont: a DatePicker inside a Modal whose only question is the day
antiPatterns.why: the picker's calendar opens a popover over the dialog; the day is the dialog's whole content, so show the month

antiPatterns.dont: a Calendar without bounds for a day that has them
antiPatterns.why: an unbounded month lets someone pick yesterday and learn only on save that it was never possible
